subject: Route-level cost + latency explorer request and SLA-exception playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: route-level cost/latency explorer + SLA-exception playbook

Hey team,

We had a follow-up with OrbitRetail earlier this week where a specific customer route saw repeated tail-latency spikes and incurred a temporary SLA credit. Sam (copied below) asked for two things we should prioritize:

1) A per-route cost + latency explorer in Console that lets CS and customers quickly slice by: customer (tenant), model, route, time-window, and token buckets. Must include percentile latency (p50/p95/p99), per-token cost, and a way to compare to baseline model variants.

2) An internal SLA-exception playbook and mutual-action plan template that we can run during these incidents: quick detection signals, guardrail runbooks (fallback routes/model variants), comms templates, and suggested remedial billing adjustments.

Attached is a short summary of the OrbitRetail incident (sla_incident_summary.pdf) — it highlights the route name, approximate spike windows, and the customer impact.

Asks:
- Dylan: can Platform produce a lightweight sketch of the data surfaces required (metric names, retention constraints, minimum query latency targets) and a rough estimate for engineering effort?
- Markus: can you advise on product prioritization and minimal ship criteria for a v1 route explorer (internal-only vs customer-facing)?
- Neha / CS: can you capture what customer-facing fields would be most useful for proactive support?

Timing: OrbitRetail expects a tentative plan by EOW (end of next week). If we need to escalate to a leadership tradeoff, flag it here.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Ops (Console & Observability) | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0197

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: route-level cost/latency explorer + SLA-exception playbook

Soojin —

Thanks for the clear ask and the incident brief. Quick notes from infra-side:

- We already emit route-level p50/p95/p99 and token counts to our metrics cluster, but the current retention for per-route histograms is short (7d) and indices are heavy. We can extend retention for specific tenant-route pairs but it will cost ~5–8% more storage on metrics infra depending on sample rates.

- For a responsive explorer, the key is pre-aggregations for common windows and a lightweight cache for recent queries (last 24–72h). I sketched a data surface in the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/route-explorer-proposals (see per-route-metrics-dump.csv for column examples).

- Effort estimate (very rough): 3–4 Sprints across 2 engs to wire an internal-only dashboard that reads from our metrics indices + a small API layer to compute per-token cost. Customer-facing rollout will add security checks and RBAC (another 2 Sprints).

- Short-term mitigation during incidents: enable automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant (we already have the routing fallback hooks) and populate a temporary CSV with per-route token counts for billing reconciliation.

I can produce a one-page engineering checklist by Monday. Attaching the metrics dump stub: per-route-metrics-dump.csv

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Platform Engineering (Runtime) | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@orbitretail.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: route-level cost/latency explorer + SLA-exception playbook

Thanks — good call. A few product decisions we need to make before we scope v1:

- Visibility surface: internal-only dashboard first (for CS + SRE) vs. immediate customer-facing view. Internal-first reduces security work and will let us iterate on UX faster.
- Minimum useful fields: p50/p95/p99, tokens-in, tokens-out, per-token-cost, model-version, route-id, region, and a short list of correlated events (deployments, autoscale events). If possible include a quick link to the underlying logs/traces for the selected window.
- Success criteria for v1: (a) CS can run a triage within 10 minutes of an incident, (b) Ops can identify root cause 50% faster vs today, (c) no PII exposed in customer-facing views.

Tessa — want your take on the customer comms templates and whether OrbitRetail’s ask justifies an accelerated slot in next quarter’s roadmap?

Sam — appreciate the incident summary. We’ll aim to have an internal plan and an initial playbook draft by 2026-11-12. If you can provide any additional context on which API routes and models were most affected that would help prioritize.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Redwood Console | Markus.small@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — concise next steps below (MUTUAL ACTION PLAN):

- Dylan: produce the one-page engineering checklist + estimated Sprints for internal-only v1 by Mon 2026-11-08 (Jira: OPS-2147).
- Product (Markus & me): draft v1 success criteria and scope out the UI wireframe for internal Console by 2026-11-10.
- CS (Neha & Tessa): prepare a customer comms template + a short FAQ for OrbitRetail by 2026-11-12.
- Customer (Sam): supply the affected route names and any raw logs you can share (S3 link preferred) — we’ll treat as confidential.

I'll consolidate responses into a single plan and present at the Monday triage sync. If anyone sees blocker risks (data retention or security), flag on this thread.

Regards,
Soojin
